_contract: THIS REPO OWNS THIS FILE. DatsMe vendors it verbatim to
api/tests/fixtures/owner_fields.json and pins its sha256 in the test that
reads it, so a drifted copy fails loudly and names this repo instead of
silently testing something else. Two repos cannot share a file, and two
independently-maintained copies drift exactly like the code they police.
DatsPet mints bundles, so DatsPet owns the wire cases: a new case lands
here first and is re-vendored — the same direction the bundle itself flows.
NOTE for the DatsMe side: DatsPet only ever WRITES the factory and public
cases (§2.4). The individual and group cases are here because the HOST
writes them at checkout and gift (§2.5), and both repos must agree on the

cases.case: factory — minted, not yet sold. The only thing DatsPet exports
individual — the DatsMe slug, written by the host at checkout
individual — re-stamped to a recipient after a gift
group — the normalized tag, a different namespace from a slug
_form: The canonical form `Group.normalized_tag` stores: words lowercased,
sorted, joined by '#', with NO leading '#'. Produced by the host's
tag_parser.normalize_tag_string, which is the same chokepoint group
creation and lookup go through — so 'Tennis#Detroit' and
'detroit#tennis' are one group. An earlier revision of this fixture
wrote '#black#zebra'; no group tag has ever looked like that.

cases.case: public — the only category with no subject, so the name is empty

_why: Every key here must survive a transfer untouched. `fingerprint` is the
one the spec cares about (§1.7 — DatsPet stamps it once at mint and the
HOST's later stamps must not lose it, which is a cross-repo promise);
deliberately nested so a shallow copy that flattens or drops structure

rejected.case: an unknown category must be refused, never treated as public
every category except public needs a subject
public has no subject, so a name is a contradiction
the timestamp is the wire format — UTC with a Z suffix
